name: H2O
source: NIST WebBook, water (CAS 7732-18-5): Shomate 298-500 K and enthalpy of formation, condensed phase (Chase, 1998); Antoine 344-373 K (Bridgeman and Aldrich, 1964; coefficients calculated by NIST), A raised by 2 for kPa; density at 298.15 K and 101.325 kPa from the NIST fluid properties tables.

name: H2O
source: NIST WebBook, water (CAS 7732-18-5): gas Shomate and enthalpy of formation (Chase, 1998). The fit is published for 500-1700 K and is extrapolated below 500 K; it gives 33.59 J/(mol.K) at 298.15 K against the tabulated 33.58.

name: SiO2
source: NIST WebBook, silicon dioxide (CAS 14808-60-7): alpha quartz Shomate 298-847 K and enthalpy of formation (Chase, 1998).

name: CuFeS2
source: Estimate. NIST publishes no fit for chalcopyrite; Neumann-Kopp over the NIST-JANAF element fits at 298.15 K (Cu 24.47 + Fe 25.10 + 2 S 22.70 = 94.97 J/(mol.K)), held constant. No enthalpy of formation, so it cannot take part in a reaction.

name: NaCl
source: NIST WebBook, sodium chloride (CAS 7647-14-5): solid Shomate 298-1073 K and enthalpy of formation (Chase, 1998).

name: N2
source: NIST WebBook, nitrogen (CAS 7727-37-9): gas Shomate 100-500 K (Chase, 1998). An element in its standard state, so zero enthalpy of formation, which is NIST's H.

name: O2
source: NIST WebBook, oxygen (CAS 7782-44-7): gas Shomate 100-700 K (Chase, 1998). An element in its standard state, so zero enthalpy of formation, which is NIST's H.

name: H2
source: NIST WebBook, hydrogen (CAS 1333-74-0): gas Shomate 298-1000 K (Chase, 1998). An element in its standard state, so zero enthalpy of formation, which is NIST's H.

name: Ar
source: NIST WebBook, argon (CAS 7440-37-1): gas Shomate 298-6000 K (Chase, 1998). B to E are all below 3e-7 and are left out, so cp is a constant 20.786 J/(mol.K). An element, so zero enthalpy of formation.

name: CO2
source: NIST WebBook, carbon dioxide (CAS 124-38-9): gas Shomate 298-1200 K and enthalpy of formation (Chase, 1998).

name: CO
source: NIST WebBook, carbon monoxide (CAS 630-08-0): gas Shomate 298-1300 K and enthalpy of formation (Chase, 1998).

name: CH4
source: NIST WebBook, methane (CAS 74-82-8): gas Shomate 298-1300 K and enthalpy of formation (Chase, 1998).

name: C2H6
source: NIST WebBook, ethane (CAS 74-84-0), which publishes no Shomate fit: A to C fitted by this crate exactly through the tabulated gas cp at 298.15, 400 and 500 K (52.49, 65.46, 77.94 J/(mol.K); Gurvich, Veyts, et al., 1989); do not trust it far outside 298-500 K. Enthalpy of formation from Manion, 2002.

name: C3H8
source: NIST WebBook, propane (CAS 74-98-6), which publishes no Shomate fit: A to C fitted by this crate exactly through the tabulated gas cp at 298.15, 400 and 500 K (73.60, 94.01, 112.59 J/(mol.K); Chao, 1973); do not trust it far outside 298-500 K. Enthalpy of formation from Pittam and Pilcher, 1972.

name: NH3
source: NIST WebBook, ammonia (CAS 7664-41-7): gas Shomate 298-1400 K and enthalpy of formation (Chase, 1998).

name: SO2
source: NIST WebBook, sulfur dioxide (CAS 7446-09-5): gas Shomate 298-1200 K and enthalpy of formation (Chase, 1998).

name: CH3OH
source: NIST WebBook, methanol (CAS 67-56-1), which publishes no liquid Shomate fit: cp and density at 298.15 K and 101.325 kPa from the NIST fluid properties tables, cp held constant. Enthalpy of formation from Chao and Rossini, 1965. Antoine 288.1-356.83 K (Ambrose and Sprake, 1970), A raised by 2 for kPa.

name: C2H5OH
source: NIST WebBook, ethanol (CAS 64-17-5), which publishes no liquid Shomate fit and is not in the NIST fluid tables, so no density: cp at 298.15 K from Petrov, Peshekhodov, et al., 1989, held constant. Enthalpy of formation is NIST's average of six values. Antoine 292.77-366.63 K (Ambrose and Sprake, 1970), A raised by 2 for kPa.

name: CH3COCH3
source: NIST WebBook, acetone (CAS 67-64-1), which publishes no liquid Shomate fit and is not in the NIST fluid tables, so no density: cp at 298.15 K from Malhotra and Woolf, 1991, held constant. Enthalpy of formation from Wiberg, Crocker, et al., 1991. Antoine 259.16-507.60 K (Ambrose, Sprake, et al., 1974), A raised by 2 for kPa.

name: C6H6
source: NIST WebBook, benzene (CAS 71-43-2), which publishes no liquid Shomate fit: cp and density at 298.15 K and 101.325 kPa from the NIST fluid properties tables, cp held constant. Enthalpy of formation from Roux, Temprado, et al., 2008. Antoine 287.70-354.07 K (Williamham, Taylor, et al., 1945), A raised by 2 for kPa.

name: C7H8
source: NIST WebBook, toluene (CAS 108-88-3), which publishes no liquid Shomate fit: cp and density at 298.15 K and 101.325 kPa from the NIST fluid properties tables, cp held constant. Enthalpy of formation from Roux, Temprado, et al., 2008. Antoine 308.52-384.66 K (Williamham, Taylor, et al., 1945), A raised by 2 for kPa.

name: C6H14
source: NIST WebBook, n-hexane (CAS 110-54-3), which publishes no liquid Shomate fit: cp and density at 298.15 K and 101.325 kPa from the NIST fluid properties tables, cp held constant.
